chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Smallens tries to throw him out at dress rehearsal
summary: Conductor Alexander Smallens threatens to throw him out for missing a downbeat; Gershwin calls him a black Toscanini and Bubbles teases Smallens into calm.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: In 1935 when I was chosen to do the Sportin' Life character of "Porgy and Bess."
Could you start over one more time?

It was in 1935 when I was chosen by the immortal George Gershwin to do the character of Sportin' Life in his new folk opera "Porgy and Bess," at the Alvin Theater in New York City in 1935 and we were to rehearse in different places, the show before and the show going on, naturally, as you might know and we did and it was on the dress rehearsal night when Alexander Smallens had decided that I wouldn't fit the show, because he had given me a down beat and I didn't take it, I was right behind his beat and he threw the baton down and says, "Throw him out! Throw him out! Take him out!" and Gersh was sitting in the back of the theater. He rushed down the aisle and says, "What's the matter? What's the matter?" And Alexander Smallens says, "Throw him out!" He says, "We can't throw him out, he's a black Toscanini, George Gershwin says to Alexander Smallens, and Alexander Smallens, when Gershwin started to the back of the theater to his seat, Alexander Smallens picked up his

baton to start to conduct and just as he stepped before the orchestra to conduct, I stepped over the footlights and said, "Mr. Smallens, if I had the money for the way you conduct, I'd be a millionaire," which made him feel more in keeping with going along with me. But Gershwin knew I could do the numbers, I could do the entire show. That's why he picked me.
